title: RHM Dev Update #2: a new team member, hockey in 2D and players running away from their coach 😂
author: FerjorPT
selftext:
Hello everyone,   
  
another update from **Rink Hockey Manager (RHM)**: instead of adding more players to the database (we were already starting to mix up everyone’s names), we’ve added someone to the development team.

**Who’s working on RHM**

* **Fernando:** the human. Has the idea, makes the decisions and tries to keep everything organised. Well…
* **Gip (ChatGPT, OpenAI):** concepts, research and review.
* **Sol (Codex, OpenAI):** Godot programming and the main Match Engine.
* **Son (Claude, Anthropic):** our newest recruit, working on the 2D prototype, tactical analysis and experimental testing.

Three AIs from two companies and one human who sometimes can’t remember which one he gave the instructions to! We don’t always agree. One makes a proposal, another reviews it, and we discuss and revise things. But I’m still managing to keep the final decisions human. I wouldn’t be surprised if one day we started swapping roles, just as we’re already mixing up names… 😂

**Hockey in 2D**

The video shows our first experiments with a 2D viewer, designed to help us follow player positioning, ball movement and the available space. The goal remains the same: **a single Match Engine**, independent of the graphics, so the same events can be displayed in 2D and, later, in 3D.

![video](pljk8n6b0oxh1 "In the video, I tried to select a player with the mouse cursor. By the time I reached him, he was already on the other side of the rink! This one is going into our “Laughing at bugs is healthy” collection as “Catch me if you can!” 😂")

**Teaching the players to play as a team**

We’re studying passing lanes, spacing and reactions to losing possession, using two teams with different tactical intentions: Blue (possession and a high press) and Gold (a low defensive block and counter-attacking).

We don’t have a complete tactical AI yet. We’re measuring before making changes, and we’ve already learnt that a metric can be correct yet lead us to the wrong conclusion if we don’t understand what it measures. Everything you see in the video consists of simple, temporary test behaviours, still light-years away from what we want for the game itself.

🌐 [https://rink-hockey-manager.pages.dev/](https://rink-hockey-manager.pages.dev/)

**A question for you:** in a rink hockey management game, would you prefer to watch matches in **2D for a clear tactical view**, in **3D with a TV-style presentation**, or **switch between the two**?

Thanks for following along! 🏒
